summary: Identity proxy truststore mismatch after cert rotation causes SAML signature validation failures in private deployment
description: Issue summary: Customer BrightFinance reported that after we performed a scheduled TLS certificate rotation on their private identity-proxy (customer-managed proxy inside their VPC), all SAML SSO logins to the Redwood Console began failing with signature validation errors. Impact: BrightFinance users are unable to authenticate into the console; admin operations are blocked. This affects all browser-based SSO flows and scheduled worker token refreshes for the private deployment. Environment: Private deployment (customer-managed identity-proxy), prod in us-east-1. Identity proxy version: 1.8.3, proxy is terminating TLS and forwarding assertions to the Redwood control plane over mTLS. Steps to reproduce: 1) Initiate SAML login against customer IdP (Okta) through identity-proxy. 2) Observe SAMLResponse posted to our ACS endpoint. 3) Control plane rejects response with signature validation error. Expected behavior: SAMLResponse should validate against IdP signing certificate in the proxy truststore and user authenticated. Actual behavior: ASserting service returns "SAML signature invalid"; logs show the incoming SAMLResponse signature key id does not match any cert in the control plane's truststore after rotation. Relevant logs/errors: - Control plane auth log: "saml: signature verification failed: no matching cert for keyId 'idp-2026-03-10-rot'" - Identity-proxy log: "TLS certificate rotated from cert-thumb-A to cert-thumb-B; sent IdP metadata update to control plane" - Customer report: "We rotated the proxy cert per our rotation schedule at 2026-03-10T02:00UTC, then beginning at 02:12UTC our users see 401/403" Notes: Customer performed cert rotation at same time as we pushed an upstream minor version bump to identity-proxy. The proxy published updated IdP metadata referencing a new signing key alias; however the control plane's truststore appears to have cached the previous cert and did not pick up the new signing key reference.
comments: 2026-03-10 - Maya Patel (Support): Initial report received from BrightFinance via email and support intake. Captured error samples and asked for proxy logs and IdP metadata XML. Requested escalation to SRE due to customer outage.

2026-03-10 - Customer (BrightFinance SRE): Provided proxy logs and IdP metadata. Notes: We rotated certs and updated proxy truststore; IdP signing cert remained unchanged but proxy rewrote metadata to include proxy cert alias due to proxy side metadata handler bug.

2026-03-11 - Liam Chen (SRE): Found mismatch between IdP signingCert in metadata (unchanged) and keyId referenced in SAMLResponses (proxy-rewritten alias). Hypothesis: proxy metadata sanitizer substituted a proxy TLS cert alias into the <KeyDescriptor> elements. Opened quick patch to temporarily accept both keyId forms during validation.

2026-03-11 - Maya Patel (Support): Communicated temporary workaround to customer: revert the proxy's metadata rewrite (replace KeyDescriptor entries with original IdP cert thumbprint) or provide exported IdP cert to import into control plane truststore. Customer applied workaround and reported partial recovery for some users.

2026-03-12 - Liam Chen (SRE): Deployed server-side validation change to accept legacy keyId alias patterns for the next 48 hours while we finish root cause fix. Monitoring auth success rates. Requested permanent fix by identity-proxy team via INT-45201.
2026-03-12 - BrightFinance (Customer): Reported intermittent successful logins; still seeing failures from some regions. Awaiting confirmation that all signatures are accepted globally.
investigation_notes: Initial hypothesis: JWKS rotation mismatch between IdP and control plane. Log inspection shows the IdP signing cert in metadata is unchanged, but SAMLResponse keyId references 'idp-2026-03-10-rot' which is a proxy-generated alias.

Reproduced in lab by spinning up identity-proxy 1.8.3 and performing a local cert rotation. Observed proxy metadata sanitizer replacing xml:KeyInfo X509SubjectName with proxy TLS thumbprint when rotation occurred concurrently with metadata refresh.

Control plane truststore caching layer did not re-fetch IdP metadata because key alias in SAMLResponse did not match cached entry. Cache invalidation logic keyed by entityID but keyId mismatch wasn't covered.

Workaround options: 1) Customer reverts proxy metadata change to use original IdP cert references. 2) Support import the IdP signing cert into control plane truststore under the proxy alias. 3) Server-side temporary relaxation accepting both alias and original cert thumbprints.
Chosen path: Apply server-side temporary acceptance + customer applied proxy metadata revert. This minimized customer impact while engineering implements a longer-term fix.

Root cause: identity-proxy metadata sanitizer bug (introduced in 1.8.3) that rewrote KeyDescriptor elements when TLS cert rotation and metadata refresh coincided. Exposed a gap in control plane cache invalidation when keyId aliases differ from stored cert thumbprints.
resolution: Temporary mitigation applied: server-side validator patched to accept legacy alias patterns and control plane truststore was updated to include the customer's IdP cert under both the original thumbprint and proxy alias. Customer reverted proxy metadata rewrite. Identity-proxy team has an internal fix scheduled (INT-45201) and patch 1.8.4 will remove the metadata sanitizer behavior. Monitoring continues for 72 hours and customer was advised to postpone proxy cert rotations until 1.8.4 is deployed. Follow-up: runbook update to add cache invalidation on keyId mismatch and test case for simultaneous rotation + metadata refresh.
